value: temperatures selected in a laboratory thermal gradient: 38.1 C in October, 33.2 C in July, 36.2 C in May
units: categorical (selected body temperature, C, in a laboratory thermal gradient, by season)

source.authors: Emmanouela Karameta, Ioanna Gavriilidi, Spyros Sfenthourakis, Panayiotis Pafilis
source.title: Seasonal Variation in the Thermoregulation Pattern of an Insular Agamid Lizard

method: behavioural thermal-gradient choice: single wild-caught adult males in a 15 to 60 C laboratory gradient, cloacal body temperature logged every 5 min for 5 h
conditions: Wild adult males (SVL above 85 mm; females excluded to avoid gravidity effects on body temperature) caught on stone walls around Demetra's temple in Sagri, Naxos, Greece (37.029 N, 25.431 E), in fieldwork in May, July and October 2017, then moved to the Department of Biology laboratories, University of Athens, and housed singly in 60 x 30 x 40 cm terraria (sand substrate, tile shelter and basking spot, 60 W incandescent lamp 8 h a day, natural photoperiod through windows, room held at 25 C, mealworms with multivitamin powder every other day, water ad libitum). Gradient: 100 x 25 x 25 cm terrarium with a 100 W and a 60 W heating lamp and two ice bags at opposite ends; each lizard was allowed to thermoregulate for an hour before the trial; a type K thermocouple taped to the back kept the probe in the cloaca, readings every 5 min for 5 h between 10:00 and 15:00. Tpref sample N = 13 males in spring (May), 11 in summer (July), 8 in autumn (October), a total of 32 trials; the captive acclimation period before testing is not stated beyond the one hour in the gradient. Statistics (Section 3.1): one-way ANCOVA on individual mean Tpref with body weight and SVL as covariates, F2,27 = 15.290, p < 0.001; Tukey HSD showed Tpref in summer differed from both other seasons (p < 0.05) while spring and autumn did not differ (p = 0.123). The Discussion gives set-point (Tset) ranges of 34.9 to 37.7 C in spring, 30.4 to 36.3 C in summer and 37.0 to 39.5 C in autumn (summer breadth doubled). The quote does not label the three figures as means; the paper elsewhere describes them as the seasonal mean Tpref values (Table 1 not read). No non-responders or other exclusions are reported. Fieldwork complied with Hellenic Presidential Decree 67/81 and EU Directive 2010/63/EU; no permit number printed.
where: Section 4 Discussion, second sentence of the paragraph beginning 'The profound effect of seasonality'
quote: Lizards selected significantly higher temperatures in October (38.1 °C), lower temperatures in the hot summer month of July (33.2 °C), and intermediate values in May (36.2 °C).
note: Sentence read in two abutting pieces from the MDPI page ('Lizards selected significantly higher temperatures in October (38.1 °C),' and 'lower temperatures in the hot summer month of July (33.2 °C), and intermediate values in May (36.2 °C).'); the previous sentence ends 'of preferred temperatures (Tpref).' and the next begins 'The same tendency was observed in Tset', so both ends are verified. The paper names the species Laudakia stellio; Reptile Database lists Laudakia stellio as the current name (Stellagama stellio only as a synonym) with Family Agamidae and Order Squamata.
